findings.F1: The move per case is far too small to pay for a trade, so the book loses before any choice of sizing. The idea's total move is +0.05 % per case over 2 hours, which is 0.2 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. The book made 65 566 trades, a median of 120 minutes each, averaging −0.078 % before fees and −0.178 % after. Sharpe was −3.97, the mean daily return on days in a position −0.2 %, and the yearly return −51.9 %.
findings.F2: The short side loses before fees and the long side carries all the gross gain. SHORT trades averaged −0.303 % gross (−0.403 % net, 32 573 trades). LONG trades averaged +0.144 % gross (+0.044 % net, 32 993 trades). At the 00:00 and 16:00 settlements over 8 hours, a fall into settlement in the 50–95th percentile of |pre-move| was followed by +21.5 bp and +23.1 bp total (unusual +16.8 bp, t 4.13, n 5 007; +18.5 bp, t 2.83, n 2 559). A rise in the same bands was followed by only +4.4 bp and +2.9 bp, and by −0.5 bp to +3.7 bp over 16 hours.
findings.F3: The effect on the long side grows with the horizon past the 2 hours the book holds, and with the size of the fall, until the extreme 1 %. For falls into settlement on the long side, the total move was:
findings.F4: The 08:00 UTC settlement carries none of the effect.
findings.F5: The move reverses when it runs against the coin's 24-hour trend, the crowded-side reading the brief gives, and it grows with the strength of that trend.
findings.F6: The settlement clock adds most in the middle band of falls. Falls in the 50–80th percentile at hours away from settlement gave +7.2 bp total and +2.6 bp unusual over 8 hours. At the 00:00 and 16:00 settlements the same band gave +21.5 bp and +16.8 bp. In the 80–95 band other hours gave +19.9 bp, close to settlement's +23.1 bp.
findings.F7: The long-side gain at 00:00 and 16:00 over 8 hours, 50–99th percentile of falls, is positive in 7 of 8 years. It ranges from +4.9 bp in 2025 to +44.5 bp in 2018; 2022 was the exception at −15.9 bp (n about 1 000–1 200 per year). So it does not rest on one period.
findings.F8: The book's gross gain sits entirely in the first 2 hours after settlement, at +0.38 and +0.75 bp per bar with a mean |allocation| of 0.43. The other six hours hold about 0.014 and earn about 0. The book pays the full cost every 8 hours for a 2-hour move, and that move is below the cost.

ideas.idea: The return over the 24 hours after the 00:00 and 16:00 UTC funding settlement times runs opposite to a fall over the 2 hours before it: the coin rises after falling into settlement, and the larger the fall against the coin's usual 2-hour move, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A fall into a 00:00 or 16:00 settlement is a reason to be long for the following day, sized by the fall; a rise into settlement is not a reason to short.
ideas.name: settlement fall recovers over day

ideas.idea: The return over the 8 hours after each funding settlement time runs opposite to the return over the 2 hours before it when that pre-move runs against the coin's 24-hour trend, and the stronger the 24-hour trend, the larger the move back.
ideas.consequence: A trader takes the reversal bet at settlement only when the move into settlement goes against the recent trend, and sizes it by the trend's strength, holding it through the 8 hours to the next settlement.
ideas.name: counter-trend settlement move reverses

ideas.idea: The return over the 8 hours after the 00:00 and 16:00 UTC funding settlement times runs opposite to a fall over the 2 hours before it, and the larger the fall against the coin's usual 2-hour move, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader keeps the long reversal on these two settlements and holds it until the next settlement, instead of paying a full trade's cost for a 2-hour move at every settlement.
ideas.name: settlement fall rebound eight hours
